name: RedSun (CVE-2026-41091) — Windows Defender Privilege Escalation Zero-Day
description: RedSun is the second of three Windows Defender zero-days disclosed within roughly two weeks by researcher 'Chaotic Eclipse', published April 15, 2026 in the GitHub repo Nightmare-Eclipse/RedSun. It exploits a logic flaw in how Defender handles cloud-tagged placeholder files: rather than quarantining or deleting a detected malicious file, Defender can rewrite or restore it to its original location with elevated privileges. Combined with NTFS directory junctions, opportunistic locks, and Cloud Files API tricks, an attacker can redirect that privileged restore operation to overwrite protected system files and obtain SYSTEM access on fully patched Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server 2019+. Huntress documented the first real-world exploitation in mid-April 2026, and the flaw remained unpatched for roughly six weeks despite active exploitation before Microsoft addressed it as CVE-2026-41091 in Defender Engine version 1.1.26040.8 on May 19, 2026. RedSun forms part of the same 'Defender becomes the door' disclosure wave as BlueHammer and UnDefend.

mitre_techniques.notes: Exploits CVE-2026-41091, a logic flaw in Defender's cloud-file restore handling, to gain SYSTEM

mitre_techniques.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
mitre_techniques.notes: Abuses Defender's own privileged 'restore from quarantine' action as the escalation primitive
NTFS directory junctions redirect Defender's privileged file restore to overwrite protected system paths
Cloud-tagged placeholder files crafted to trigger the vulnerable Defender code path

notable_examples: April 15, 2026: Proof-of-concept published in GitHub repo Nightmare-Eclipse/RedSun, the second of three Defender zero-days from the same researcher in two weeks
Mid-April 2026: Huntress incident responders documented the first confirmed real-world exploitation
Remained unpatched for roughly six weeks despite active exploitation before Microsoft shipped Defender Engine 1.1.26040.8 on May 19, 2026 (CVE-2026-41091)
Forms part of the BlueHammer / RedSun / UnDefend trio of Defender-abuse zero-days disclosed in a six-week span
detection_opportunities: Update Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform/Engine to version 1.1.26040.8 or later
Monitor for Cloud Files API (cldflt.sys) activity combined with NTFS junction creation by non-SYSTEM processes
Alert on Defender 'restore from quarantine' actions targeting protected system directories
Apply interim mitigations (e.g. Qualys guidance) for hosts pending the May 2026 Defender engine update
Hunt for SYSTEM-level process creation immediately following Defender scan-triggered file operations
